stem:
Eshan visits a dry sandy yard with cactus and a cool shady wall with ferns. He asks why the plants in the two places differ.

Which claims are correct? One or more options may be correct.

options.text: Different conditions of water, heat, and soil support different plants in the two places.
The plants found in a region depend on the living conditions there.
The dry yard is dry because cactus and ferns made it dry.
No plant can ever live in both a dry yard and a cool shady place.

teacher.key_rationale: Regional plant and animal differences follow from different living conditions. Saying the plants caused the dryness reverses cause and effect; saying no kind can live in both places overextends collection-level differences.
